records.name: Chloe's Way
records.summary: A community nonprofit that helps families and individuals in hardship with food boxes, clothing, and hygiene kits. It also runs summer lunch help and a youth summer program, and it offers scholarships to high school seniors.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers help with summer lunch support (meal help, set-up, and clean-up) and with the youth summer enrichment program for 4th to 6th graders. Donors can give through the donate page.

schedule.text: Summer lunch support and youth summer enrichment run in the summer, but the page gives no exact dates. Scholarships and prom help are yearly.

cost.text: Help is free; donations are welcome

first_step.how: Email kera@chloesway.org to ask how to volunteer for summer lunch or the youth summer enrichment program.
first_step.basis: The site invites volunteers and gives a contact email, although its volunteer button is still a placeholder.

records.notes: The newest dated item is a scholarship deadline of March 31, 2026, shown on the homepage. The news headlines there are undated. The footer lists a second email, support@chloesway.org. Impact counters show zero, so no figures are published here. IRS address (5428 Florence Ave) is not published; zip only. Legal name: Chloes Way.

records.name: Creative Arts and Healing Enterprises
records.summary: An arts and healing group led by Philadelphia artist Terrence Gore. It has a workshop section, posts about its events, and takes donations.
records.what_you_do: Take part in the group's workshops or events, which are named on its site. Use the contact form there to ask how to join a workshop.

first_step.how: Send a message through the contact form on terrencelgore.com to ask about upcoming workshops.
first_step.basis: Workshops are named on the site, but no dates or sign-up steps are shown, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: Legal name: Creative Arts and Healing Enterprises (the IRS spelling splits 'Enterprises'). The donate button goes to a GiveLively page under that name. The 'Art of Healing' and 'Rehabilitation' workshop pages were named, but no dated sessions were visible. A guessed /workshop address returned 404. The medium of the workshops is not stated, so the interests are the closest fit. The contact email looks personal; check it before showing. Newest dated item: an Oct 1, 2025 post.

records.name: Djola History and Genealogy Society
records.summary: A history and genealogy society for people whose African ancestry DNA results link them to the Djola family. It shares Djola history, oral histories, and research on DNA, places, and language.
records.what_you_do: Join as a member through the society's Become a Member page, or sign up for its newsletter to hear about news and events.

schedule.text: Listed hours: Monday to Friday, 6:30 to 9 pm, and Saturday and Sunday, 8 am to 6 pm (Eastern time). No events are dated on the page.

cost.text: Dues and membership costs are not stated on the page.

first_step.how: Sign up for the newsletter on djola.org, or use the Become a Member page to ask how to join.
first_step.basis: The site has a membership page and a newsletter form, but it does not explain what membership involves or whether visits are open.

records.notes: The site works but shows no dated news or events, so status is probably_active under the no-dates rule. Legal name: Djola History and Genealogy Society in America Incorporated. The IRS address is an apartment, so only the zip is listed. Djola is not in the heritage list, so audience.community is left empty. Membership terms are unknown.

records.name: Greenest
records.summary: Runs Greentool, an online tool for tracking the environmental effects of products, services, and companies. Volunteer analysts research and edit the data through its portal.
records.what_you_do: Apply for a volunteer analyst role through the careers listings on greenest.org to help with the data. Anyone can also suggest a business or product for review without doing research.

first_step.how: Apply for a volunteer analyst role through the careers listings on greenest.org.
first_step.basis: Volunteers apply for a role, so the way in is an application step rather than an open drop in.

records.notes: This is an online volunteer program with no local meetings or Philadelphia-specific programs seen, so the owner may want to decide whether an online national project belongs in a Philadelphia directory. The IRS address is in Philadelphia (an apartment, not published). The homepage has no dated news; its only date is a 2025 copyright footer, which is not evidence. Legal name: Greenest Inc. The tool is Greentool.

records.name: Holobiont Laboratory
records.summary: A community lab based at Karakung Reef in West Philadelphia that tests climate ideas with neighbors. Its projects include solar installs, a heat shelter with solar-powered sprinklers, and hands-on solar and papermaking sessions.
records.what_you_do: Come to the lab's public events, such as the off-grid solar session (date to be announced) or a zine launch party. Subscribe to its email updates to hear when new events are scheduled.

schedule.text: Events are posted as they are planned. Dated items seen: a zine launch party on Feb 28, 2026, and a Lab Notes entry for a May 6 papermaking workshop with no year given. An off-grid solar session is listed with no date.

first_step.how: Subscribe to email updates through the link on holobiontlab.org, then come to the next open event.
first_step.basis: Events are listed publicly and an email update sign-up is offered; no application is mentioned.

records.notes: Legal name: Holobiont Laboratory. The site says the Feb 28, 2026 zine party was at 915 Spring Garden. The mailing PO box is not published. No email or phone is published on the site. The May 6 papermaking workshop has no year, so it does not set the status.

records.name: Human Rights Coalition
records.summary: A grassroots group run by people in prison and their families. It campaigns against solitary confinement and harsh prison conditions, pushes for fairer sentencing and release, and helps people inside prepare for life after prison.
records.what_you_do: Join a campaign or volunteer through the Get Involved form on the site, write letters through its letter-writing work, or read its quarterly magazine, The MOVEMENT.

first_step.how: Fill in the Get Involved form on hrcoalition.org to say you want to help with a campaign.
first_step.basis: The site has a clear public sign-up form for campaigns and volunteering, and no application is mentioned.

records.notes: The newest dated item is a 2025 impact summary with no month, so last_sign_of_life is left out and status is probably_active. The page lists no public meetings or events. The mailing PO box is not published. Legal name: Human Rights Coalition.

records.name: Irvin Kelly Foundation
records.summary: Helps veterans who are moving back into civilian life with stable housing and job placement, and offers scholarships for descendants of service members.
records.what_you_do: Ask for help with housing, employment, or scholarship information through the contact form on the site or by email. The site does not list volunteer roles or events.

first_step.how: Use the contact form on irvinkellyfoundation.org, or email support@irvinkellyfoundation.org, to ask about housing or job help.
first_step.basis: The site gives a public contact form and email for help requests, and no membership or dues are mentioned.

records.notes: Legal name: Irvin Kelly Foundation NP. The name says Foundation, but the site describes its own housing and career programs, so it is treated as a service charity rather than a private grantmaker; the owner may want to confirm the IRS status. The fetched page was cut short, so later sections were not read. No dated items seen, so status is probably_active. The phone number is recorded as published. Veteran eligibility is not spelled out, so open_to is public and community is veterans.

notes: Budget: both WebSearch calls used (cap reached), 28 of 60 fetches used. Verdicts: publish 13 (9 with full records; 4 are unknown placeholders with no summary, so the pipeline will hold them back), out_of_area 1 (Green Book), not_a_group 1 (John Graves Productions). Fetch failures: arce-pa (connection closed on all 3 tries, www and bare host) and erfoundation19.com (empty page on all 3 tries, www and bare host). Both are recorded as unknown, not invented. 404s: fortressarts.org (both hosts), a guessed terrencelgore.com/workshop path, and a guessed letscircleup.org/contact path. Bria Young's website does not resolve (DNS failure), so one search was used; the 6abc Safe Summer article is dated June 11, 2022, which makes the group dormant. Green Book: the batch's liveness block said newest_date 2026-05 from sitemap.xml; I did not verify that and used the March 2026 date seen on the page. Chloe's Way's newest date is a March 31, 2026 scholarship deadline. Several IRS groups have apartment addresses, so only zips are published for them. All summaries were written in our own words.
